title: Examples
text: First define helpers. Data simulation search order use Julia’s random number generator, set.seed() control, set_seeds() seeds . Run examples order shown reproduce output. figure shows, every criterion, value number selected variables search step: solid lines n=1000n = 1000 dotted lines n=2000n = 2000. Light grey vertical lines mark new pass predictors, dashed line marks true model size. Criteria larger penalties take lower values, compare shapes curves, heights. script data-raw/readme_figures.R package source runs code section redraws figures.
code: set_seeds <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   JuliaCall::julia_command(sprintf("import Random; Random.seed!(%d);", seed)) }  criteria <- c(AIC = "Calculate_AIC", BIC = "Calculate_BIC", GIC6 = "Calculate_GIC6") sample_sizes <- c(n1000 = 1000, n2000 = 2000)  # Run the search once per criterion, on the first n observations for each n compare_criteria <- function(X, Y, init, k, Nsim) {   lapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {     Xn <- X[1:n, ]     Yn <- if (is.matrix(Y)) Y[1:n, , drop = FALSE] else Y[1:n]     lapply(criteria, function(crit)       GICSelection(Xn, Yn, init, crit, paste0(crit, "_short"), k = k, Nsim = Nsim))   }) }  last_model <- function(fit) sort(fit$selected_coeffs[[length(fit$selected_coeffs)]])  # Size, false positives and false negatives of each final model selection_table <- function(fits, truth) {   rows <- lapply(fits, function(by_crit) t(sapply(by_crit, function(fit) {     s <- last_model(fit)     c(size = length(s), false_pos = length(setdiff(s, truth)),       false_neg = length(setdiff(truth, s)))   })))   out <- do.call(rbind, rows)   rownames(out) <- paste(rep(names(fits), each = length(criteria)), rownames(out))   out }

title: Examples
text: Take n=2000n = 2000 p=500p = 500, 5 true coefficients equal 2 noise set signal--noise ratio β⊤Σβ/σ2=0.71\beta^\top\Sigma\beta/\sigma^2 = 0.71. Start every search full model: GIC6 selects exactly 5 true predictors sample sizes. BIC keeps 5 adds 3 noise variables n=1000n = 1000 4 n=2000n = 2000: doubling nn help, penalty ignores 500 candidates. AIC keeps 200 variables either size.
code: set_seeds(1) n <- 2000; p <- 500 X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p) true_cols <- sort(sample(p, 5)) beta <- numeric(p); beta[true_cols] <- 2 Y <- LP_to_Y(X, beta, family = "Normal", std = sqrt(sum(beta^2) / 0.71))  fits <- compare_criteria(X, Y, 1:p, k = p, Nsim = 5) selection_table(fits, true_cols) #>            size false_pos false_neg #> n1000 AIC   230       225         0 #> n1000 BIC     8         3         0 #> n1000 GIC6    5         0         0 #> n2000 AIC   197       192         0 #> n2000 BIC     9         4         0 #> n2000 GIC6    5         0         0

title: Examples
text: Five responses, 5 predictors coefficients 10 0.1. Pass n×5n \times 5 response matrix Y: Two responses share predictor, 24 predictors truly active. BIC GIC6 select noise variables either sample size. Every predictor miss (4 BIC, 5 GIC6) coefficient 0.1, small detect 1000 2000 observations. AIC finds 24 n=2000n = 2000, inside model 232 variables.
code: m <- 5 B <- matrix(0, p, m) true_by_response <- vector("list", m) for (i in 1:m) {   cols <- sort(sample(p, 5))   true_by_response[[i]] <- cols   B[cols, i] <- seq(10, 0.1, length.out = 5) } Y_multi <- LP_to_Y(X, B, family = "MultivariateNormal", cov_matrix = diag(m)) true_union <- sort(unique(unlist(true_by_response)))  fits <- compare_criteria(X, Y_multi, 1:p, k = p, Nsim = 5) selection_table(fits, true_union) #>            size false_pos false_neg #> n1000 AIC   268       245         1 #> n1000 BIC    20         0         4 #> n1000 GIC6   19         0         5 #> n2000 AIC   232       208         0 #> n2000 BIC    20         0         4 #> n2000 GIC6   19         0         5

title: Performance
text: Every criterion package depends data quantities least-squares fit selected columns XSX_S: Y⊤HY=b⊤Mb,RSS=Y⊤Y−Y⊤HY,b=XS⊤Y,M=(XS⊤XS)−1. Y^\top H Y = b^\top M b, \qquad \mathrm{RSS} = Y^\top Y - Y^\top H Y, \qquad b = X_S^\top Y, \quad M = (X_S^\top X_S)^{-1}.  n×nn \times n hat matrix HH never formed. search keeps MM bb current model scores proposed move rank-one update. Adding column xzx_z: u=XS⊤xzu = X_S^\top x_z, s=xz⊤xz−u⊤Mus = x_z^\top x_z - u^\top M u e=xz⊤Y−b⊤Mue = x_z^\top Y - b^\top M u, Y⊤HY→Y⊤HY+ee⊤/s.Y^\top H Y \;\\; Y^\top H Y + e\,e^\top / s . Removing column jj: β̂j=(Mb)j\hat\beta_j = (M b)_j, Y⊤HY→Y⊤HY−β̂j⊤β̂j/Mjj.Y^\top H Y \;\\; Y^\top H Y - \hat\beta_j^\top \hat\beta_j / M_{jj} . Scoring move costs O(nK+K2)O(nK + K^2) model KK variables, MM updated move accepted. Version 0.1.2 rebuilt HH every proposal, O(n2K)O(n^2 K) cost per move.

what: Fast Variable Selection with Information Criteria
title: Fast Variable Selection with Information Criteria
text: GICHighDimension R package variable selection high-dimensional regression. searches subsets predictors one maximizes generalized information criterion (GIC), AIC, BIC, EBIC GIC2–GIC6, using fast Hopfield-network style coordinate search. Univariate multivariate responses supported, along common generalized linear model families. search engine written Julia called R JuliaCall. never forms n×nn \times n hat matrix: every proposed move scored rank-one update, pass thousands candidate predictors takes milliseconds. method described Xiao Walker (2026).

title: GIC-Based Variable Selection — GICSelection
text: Performs variable selection using Generalized Information Criterion (GIC) Hopfield Network optimization. computationally intensive components implemented 'Julia' performance, 'R' interface provides user-friendly access.

title: GIC-Based Variable Selection — GICSelection
code: GICSelection(X, Y, Initial_Column, Calculate_GIC, Calculate_GIC_short, k,              Nsim = 1L, gamma = 0.6)

title: GIC-Based Variable Selection — GICSelection
text: X Numeric design matrix (n x p), n number observations p number predictors. Y Numeric response (either vector length n matrix n rows). Initial_Column Integer vector initial feature indices consider. Calculate_GIC Character name 'Julia' function full GIC calculation. Calculate_GIC_short Character name matching _short 'Julia' function. Kept backward compatibility; built-criteria use fast rank-one updates instead. k Integer model-size cap: move give model k variables skipped. Models also never exceed \(n - 1\) variables (\(n\) = sample size), selected models min(k, n) - 1 variables. Nsim Integer number passes variables, new random order (default: 1). gamma EBIC tuning constant \(\gamma\) (default 0.6); ignored criteria.

text: list containing: GIC_values: Calculated GIC values candidate models selected_coeffs: Indices selected variables

title: Information Criterion Calculations via Julia — information_criteria
text: Every criterion form \(Y^\top H Y / n - p(n, K)\), \(H\) hat matrix \(K\) selected columns \(p(n, K)\) penalty (Xiao Walker, 2026). \(\hat\sigma^2 = \mathrm{RSS}/(n - K)\) \(P\) number candidate predictors, supported criteria : AIC, Akaike information criterion (Akaike, 1974): \(K\hat\sigma^2/n\). AICc, AIC corrected small samples (Hurvich Tsai, 1989): \((K+1)\hat\sigma^2/(n-K-2)\). BIC, Bayesian information criterion (Schwarz, 1978): \(K\hat\sigma^2\log(n)/n\). CAIC, consistent AIC (Bozdogan, 1987): \(K\hat\sigma^2(\log n + 1)/n\). CAICF, consistent AIC Fisher information (Bozdogan, 1987): CAIC penalty plus \(\hat\sigma^2 \log\det(X^\top X/\hat\sigma^2)/n\). SIC, square-root information criterion (Shao, 1997; Xiao Walker, 2026): \(K\hat\sigma^2/\sqrt{n}\). GIC2–GIC6, generalized information criteria high dimensions (Kim, Kwon Choi, 2012), penalties \(K\hat\sigma^2 P^{1/3}/n\), \(2K\hat\sigma^2\log(P)/n\), \(2K\hat\sigma^2(\log P + \log\log P)/n\), \(K\hat\sigma^2\log\log(n)\log(P)/n\) \(K\hat\sigma^2\log(n)\log(P)/n\). EBIC, extended BIC (Chen Chen, 2008): \(K\hat\sigma^2\{\log n + \gamma\log\binom{P}{K}\}/n\), \(\gamma = 0.6\) default. AttIC, attention-weighted criterion specific package: fit term replaced \(Y^\top \mathrm{softmax}(HY)\) penalty SIC. Short versions (e.g., Calculate_AIC_Short) allow reusing precomputed inverse matrix save computational time.
